title: Do newborn boys weigh more than newborn girls?
description: The weights of six newborn boys and six newborn girls are compared on one dot plot. The video finds the median, the range and the mean of each group and says what the numbers show.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare two groups by their middle, their average and their spread together. Watch for students who say one group is heavier from a single baby, or who ignore that the two ranges are equal.

source: Weights of newborn boys and girls: dot plot, analyse and compare
video_script.why: The child can find a median and a mean and now uses both, with the range, to compare two groups.
video_script.substitution: Sort each group for its median and range, then share each total for its mean.
video_script.payoff_line: Boys average about three point four three kilograms and girls average three point three five kilograms.

final_answer.value: boys mean 3.43 kg, median 3.45 kg; girls mean 3.35 kg, median 3.4 kg; same spread
final_answer.spoken: boys three point four three kilograms, girls three point three five kilograms

maths_rules: boys total 20.6, mean 20.6 / 6 = 3.43 (to two decimal places)
video_script.design: One idea: compare two groups by middle, average and spread. Two rows of baby cards sit in the anchor and share one dot plot axis on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about newborn babies.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The weights of six baby boys are given in kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The weights of six baby girls are given too.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which group will weigh more, on average?

beats.on_screen: the two rows hold still and get an accent underline

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one dot plot axis from 2.4 to 4.2 kg; one dot per baby for each group; a bracket from the leftmost to the rightmost dot labelled range

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A dot plot gives each baby one dot above its weight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Both groups share one axis, so we can compare them.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The gap from the lightest to the heaviest is called the range.

marks.m1: the boys' six weights are written
marks.m2: the girls' six weights are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, six weights for the boys.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Given, six weights for the girls.

beats.on_screen: To find: median, range and mean of each group, and compare

marks.m1: the words median, range, mean and compare are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the median, the range and the mean of each group, and compare them.

marks.m2: the third and fourth cards, 3.4 and 3.5, glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, sort the boys' weights from smallest to largest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>With six weights, the middle two are three point four and three point five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Halfway between them is three point four five, so that is the median.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The range is four point one take away two point six, which is one point five kilograms.

marks.m2: the third and fourth cards, both 3.4, glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, sort the girls' weights in the same way.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The middle two are both three point four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Halfway between them is three point four, so that is the median.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The range is four take away two point five, which is also one point five kilograms.

beats.on_screen: boys total 20.6, mean = 20.6 ÷ 6; girls total 20.1, mean = 20.1 ÷ 6
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, add the boys' weights, which make twenty point six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Share that equally among six babies.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The girls' weights make twenty point one.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Share that equally among six babies as well.

marks.m1: the sorted boys' cards pair up, smallest with largest
marks.m2: the three pair sums are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the boys' total by adding in pairs.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two point six and four point one make six point seven. Three point two and three point eight make seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three point four and three point five make six point nine.
The three pairs add up to twenty point six, as before.

beats.on_screen: Answer: boys mean ≈ 3.43 kg, median 3.45 kg; girls mean 3.35 kg, median 3.4 kg; both ranges 1.5 kg

marks.m2: the two equal ranges are joined by an equals sign

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Boys average about three point four three kilograms and girls average three point three five kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The medians are three point four five and three point four, and both ranges are one point five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The spread is the same and the dots overlap a lot.
The boys are only slightly heavier on average.
